description.en-US: The historical essays Newman wrote as a Catholic, gathered in the Historical Sketches of 1872-73: nine lectures on the Turks in their relation to Europe (1853), The Mission of St. Benedict and The Benedictine Schools, the Rise and Progress of Universities, The Northmen and Normans in England and Ireland, and Medieval Oxford. The earlier Anglican pieces of the same volumes (Church of the Fathers, the Cicero and Apollonius essays, Primitive Christianity, Convocation of Canterbury) are not in this book.
description.pt-BR: Os ensaios históricos que Newman escreveu como católico, reunidos nos Historical Sketches de 1872-73: nove conferências sobre os turcos em sua relação com a Europa (1853), A Missão de São Bento e As Escolas Beneditinas, Origem e Progresso das Universidades, Os Normandos na Inglaterra e na Irlanda e Oxford Medieval. As peças anglicanas anteriores dos mesmos volumes (A Igreja dos Padres, os ensaios sobre Cícero e Apolônio, o Cristianismo Primitivo, a Convocação de Cantuária) não estão neste livro.

en-US.editor: John Henry Newman (Longmans, uniform edition, vols. 1-3; Newman Reader)

sources.edition: Historical Sketches, vols. 1-3 (London: Longmans, Green, 1872-73), as transcribed by the Newman Reader.
sources.description: 36 chapters: Newman Reader page numbers, navigation and its editorial remarks are dropped; Newman's own notes are kept as footnotes. Only the pieces written as a Catholic (1853 on). The Turks' table of dynasties (122 words) is left out. Raw page text in sources/en-US-originals/.
sources.tierEvidence: Public domain: Newman died in 1890 and the text is of a Longmans impression (or earlier edition) before 1930. The Newman Reader page footers claim copyright in the site's transcription (c) 2007 NINS; a plain transcription of a public-domain text adds no authorship under US law.
